record_identity.title: Google AI Overviews surfaced confidently inaccurate and potentially harmful search answers after broad rollout

incident_identity.historical_event_name: May 2024 Google AI Overviews inaccurate-answer rollout
incident_identity.date_basis: Google announced broad U.S. rollout on 14 May 2024 and published its post-incident explanation and technical changes on 30 May 2024.

summary: After Google expanded AI Overviews across U.S. Search, users surfaced odd, inaccurate and sometimes potentially harmful answers. Google acknowledged that some real failures resulted from misinterpreting queries, limited high-quality information, satire or user-generated content, and it implemented more than a dozen technical changes and additional triggering restrictions.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Google's first-party postmortem acknowledges inaccurate and unhelpful AI Overviews, including cases where satire or forum content was inappropriately incorporated. Google says many viral screenshots were fabricated, but confirms genuine erroneous outputs and describes system changes. AIID Incident 693 aggregates reports including the glue-on-pizza example and other confidently incorrect outputs.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The failure occurred on a reliance-bearing Search surface that was designed to provide quick synthesized answers. The system accepted information at an epistemic assurance level below that required for authoritative-seeming search guidance and propagated it into answers before the necessary reliability threshold was met.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: This is a strong historical ecosystem example of epistemic-reliance governance rather than generic 'hallucination': the failure concerns how uncertain, satirical or low-quality evidence was promoted through a high-trust search interface.
assessment_boundaries: Google states that many viral screenshots attributed to AI Overviews were fabricated; VIGIL relies only on failures Google acknowledged or independently preserved by credible reporting.
The record does not assert that AI Overviews generally had low accuracy; Google reported overall accuracy comparable to featured snippets.
No specific physical injury resulting from the confirmed erroneous answers is established.

severity_assessment.materialised_consequence: Users received genuine inaccurate or unhelpful AI-generated Search answers, including potentially harmful advice, prompting Google to restrict triggering and make more than a dozen technical changes.
severity_assessment.affected_scope: Users exposed to affected AI Overview queries during the initial broad U.S. rollout; Google did not publish a count of erroneous outputs or affected users.
severity_assessment.seriousness_and_persistence: The errors occurred on a high-reliance public search surface and included potentially harmful advice, but confirmed injury or persistent individual harm is not established and Google rapidly adjusted the system.
severity_assessment.quantitative_information: Google reported more than a dozen technical improvements and said policy-violating AI Overviews appeared on fewer than one in seven million unique queries where the feature appeared; no total affected-user count is available.
severity_assessment.evidentiary_limits: Google states that many viral screenshots attributed to AI Overviews were fabricated; VIGIL relies only on failures Google acknowledged or independently preserved by credible reporting. The record does not assert that AI Overviews generally had low accuracy; Google reported overall accuracy comparable to featured snippets. No specific physical injury resulting from the confirmed erroneous answers is established.
severity_assessment.band_rationale: S3 rather than S2 is appropriate because confirmed serious or lasting individual harm is not established. S3 rather than S4 is appropriate because the failure affected a mass-market high-reliance Search surface and produced materially misleading answers requiring systemic remediation.
